topic: Can the MoonAliza Electron desktop app sign users in to GitHub (OAuth device flow or another desktop-suited flow), to Claude with a Claude.ai subscription account, and to OpenAI Codex with Sign in with ChatGPT, and use those sign-ins for repository access and model calls - or must third-party apps use API keys
notes: Budget: at most 8 Firecrawl credits for the whole project (operator instruction, 2026-10-12). Owner pages named directly, no searches (a search costs more than a page and the owner pages are known). Run 1 collects the 7 pages below; run 2 adds the GitHub REST rate-limits page as the 8th page only if run 1 cost exactly 1 credit per page (checked with --status / doctor's balance between runs). Starting balance 290 credits. Run 1 (2026-10-12) collected 7 pages for exactly 7 credits (290 -> 283), so run 2 collects the REST rate-limits page; maxScrapes lowered to 1 for run 2 so the 7 cached pages cannot be re-fetched.

urls.why: U-1, U-4: GitHub's OAuth App authorization flows - the device flow, how it is enabled, its polling and rate limits, and the web flow's loopback redirect for desktop apps
U-2: which OAuth scope grants read access to private repositories, and whether a read-only private-repo scope exists
U-1, U-3: GitHub App user access tokens - device flow for GitHub Apps, token expiry, refresh tokens
U-5: Anthropic's statement on authentication and credential use - whether third-party products may offer Claude.ai login or use Free/Pro/Max credentials
U-5, U-6: Agent SDK authentication - API key requirement and any statement on claude.ai login in third-party products
U-7: how Codex signs in with ChatGPT versus an API key, and any statement on third-party use of ChatGPT sign-in
U-8: OpenAI's consumer Terms of Use - account sharing, automated access, and whether ChatGPT plan access may be used through third-party software

U-4: primary REST API rate limit for requests made with an OAuth app token or a GitHub App user access token (run 2, the 8th and last page of the 8-credit budget; run 1 cost exactly 7 credits, 290 -> 283)
